items.title: Why do some people feel emotionally attached to AI models
items.raw_excerpt: This feels strange to admit. I notice that sometimes I speak to AI systems like they are a friend. I know they are not real. I know there is no person on the other side. Still my brain acts like there is. I feel a small emotional connection. I see comments online saying this happens to others too. I am trying to understand if this is a new psychological effect or if humans always did this with new technology. Maybe it is the same as talking to pets or giving names to cars. Or maybe it is something deeper. Why do you think this happens. Is it loneliness. Is it empathy misfiring. Is it design tricks. Is it harmless or dangerous. I am curious how the HN crowd sees it.

items.title: Is there an AI subscription plan comparison tool that's always updated?
items.raw_excerpt: I asked versions of this question to a few different models but I never found an accurate answer. I would like to compare the various free and paid AI subscription plans, primarily from the most popular vendors like ChatGPT, Claude, Google, etc. I can find countless static webpages, YouTube videos, etc. that compare subscriptions, but their information quickly becomes out-of-date, or isn't detailed enough. I'm looking for a tool that grabs the latest information on what each plan provides (features, models, context windows, etc.), and compares them across different subscriptions. I imagine this information would be obtained from API calls or scraping. The comparison tool should not rely on AI to get its information.. I want the latest facts (ideally checked at least once a day).

excerpt_i18n.en:
Author: Bao Yonggang  Editor: Lin Juemin  
Midwinter in Beijing carries a slight chill, but the venue of Moore Threads' first developer conference (MDC) was buzzing with energy. The 1,000-square-meter exhibition area gathered over a thousand developers, who focused on cutting-edge technologies like intelligent robots, digital humans, and Agents, while also discussing advanced applications such as AI for Science and weather prediction.  
The digital entertainment and video multimedia zone at the center of the exhibition area was the most eye-catching: some were immersed in controlling the eVTOL full-motion flight simulator, while others were engaged in intense battles in classic fighting games like King of Fighters and AAA titles powered by domestic GPUs. "We might be the only ones in China currently capable of showcasing Street Fighter games," an engineer pointed out, highlighting Moore Threads' rarity in possessing both AI computing power and graphics capabilities among its peers.  
If one only learns about Moore Threads—one of the few domestic companies developing full-feature GPUs—through text or videos, it might remain an abstract concept. Being at the exhibition, with ten GPU application cases displayed at once, is enough to convey part of the GPU's value. But when nearly a hundred applications are showcased simultaneously, the impact is twofold: on one hand, it offers an intuitive understanding of the capabilities of a full-feature GPU; on the other, all these applications come from a domestic GPU company founded just five years ago.  
Moore Threads translates the capabilities of its full-feature GPU into a wide range of applications spanning from consumer to vertical industries, and from graphics to AI and high-performance computing. This not only concretely demonstrates its unique value but also allows for a tangible sense of its impact.
excerpt_i18n.es:
Autor | Bao Yonggang  Editor | Lin Juemin  
Aunque Pekín en pleno invierno tiene un ligero frío, el ambiente en la sede de la primera Conferencia de Desarrolladores de Moore Threads (MDC) era de gran calidez. En una zona de exposición de 1.000 metros cuadrados se reunieron más de mil desarrolladores, interesados en tecnologías de vanguardia como robots inteligentes, humanos digitales y agentes, además de debatir sobre aplicaciones avanzadas como la IA para la ciencia y la predicción meteorológica.  
La zona central de entretenimiento digital y multimedia fue la más llamativa: algunos se sumergían en la experiencia de controlar un simulador de vuelo completo de eVTOL, mientras otros libraban intensas batallas en mundos de juegos clásicos como "The King of Fighters" y títulos AAA impulsados por GPU nacionales. "Actualmente, quizás solo yo puedo exhibir juegos como Street Fighter en el país".

excerpt_i18n.en: Recently, the international market research firm Omdia released the "2025 Global Enterprise MaaS Market Analysis" report: as of October 2025, OpenAI and Google Cloud ranked first and second in the global MaaS service market, with daily token calls of nearly 70 trillion and 43 trillion, respectively. Chinese cloud provider Volcano Engine, with over 30 trillion daily token calls, placed third globally, capturing a 15% market share. Together, these three providers account for 65% of the global MaaS market. Currently, MaaS services have become the fastest-growing and highest-margin AI cloud computing product. Latest data from Volcano Engine shows that as of December this year, the daily call volume for the Doubao large model has exceeded 50 trillion tokens, a 66.7% increase from October and more than tenfold growth compared to the same period last year. Through technological innovations such as model architecture and software-hardware engineering optimizations, large models offer highly cost-effective services while maintaining strong margins. According to Tan Dai, President of Volcano Engine, the margin level of Doubao's large model MaaS far surpasses that of traditional cloud products like IaaS. Leading model providers continue to innovate, focusing on multimodal and Agent capabilities, thereby unlocking more application scenarios. Taking the latest flagship models as examples, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.0, and Doubao 1.8 are all multimodal large models, natively supporting visual understanding such as images, and enhancing tool invocation and multi-turn interactions.

items.raw_excerpt: 2025年12月12-13日，第八届GAIR全球人工智能与机器人大会在深圳·博林天瑞喜来登酒店正式启幕。 作为AI 产学研投界的标杆盛会，GAIR自2016年创办以来，始终坚守“传承+创新”内核，始终致力于连接技术前沿与产业实践。 在人工智能逐步成为国家竞争核心变量的当下，算力正以前所未有的速度重塑技术路径与产业结构。13日举办的「AI 算力新十年」专场聚焦智能体系的底层核心——算力，从架构演进、生态构建到产业化落地展开系统讨论，试图为未来十年的中国AI产业，厘清关键变量与发展方向。 并行科技副总裁、AI联合创始人赵鸿冰在「AI 算力新十年」论坛发表了主题为《基于用户视角的算力服务及算网服务》的演讲。 历经18年超算领域深耕，并行科技见证并参与了中国算力市场的演进。当前，算力市场呈现多场景、多业态的爆发式增长，从尖端超算到智算形态，从算力租赁到算力网络，行业生态日趋多元；与此同时，大模型技术的快速迭代，也对算力的可用性、高效性与性价比提出了更高要求。 在这样的背景下，从用户视角构建算力服务体系、通过算力网络实现资源的高效整合与调度，以及应对推理需求爆发带来的产业变革，成为算力行业亟待解决的核心问题。 赵鸿冰在演讲中指出，当前算力市场已形成四大核心业态：算力租赁作为最基础的形态，以“裸金属”算力资源长期交付用户且不参与后续应用；算力服务聚焦用户终端需求的“最后一公里”，核心是按需提供精准适配业务场景的算力支持；算力运营则依靠复杂调度平台统筹管理资源，实现算力的高效分配与运营；而算力网络作为更高维度的形态，通过纳管多个算力平台形成广泛覆盖的网络，达成跨平台整体调度。 为此，并行科技推出“厂网结合”模式：“厂”即公司投入大量资金建设的万卡集群等重资产布局，“网”则是通过轻资产扩张连接国内47个智算中心与15个超算中心，该算力网络可调度200万CPU核心、5万多张GPU卡，服务超1

excerpt_i18n.en: On December 12-13, 2025, the 8th GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit officially commenced at the Sheraton Shenzhen Boao Tianrui Hotel. As a benchmark event in the AI industry-academia-research-investment community, GAIR has consistently adhered to the core principle of "heritage + innovation" since its inception in 2016, dedicated to bridging cutting-edge technology with industrial practice. With artificial intelligence increasingly becoming a core variable in national competition, computing power is reshaping technological pathways and industrial structures at an unprecedented pace. The "AI Computing Power in the Next Decade" session held on the 13th focused on computing power—the foundational core of intelligent systems—engaging in systematic discussions from architectural evolution and ecosystem development to industrial implementation, aiming to clarify key variables and development directions for China's AI industry over the next ten years. At the "AI Computing Power in the Next Decade" forum, Zhao Hongbing, Vice President and AI Co-founder of Parallel Technology, delivered a keynote speech titled "Computing Power Services and Computing Network Services from a User Perspective." With 18 years of deep expertise in the supercomputing field, Parallel Technology has witnessed and participated in the evolution of China's computing power market. Currently, the computing power market is experiencing explosive growth across multiple scenarios and business models, ranging from cutting-edge supercomputing to intelligent computing forms, and from computing power leasing to computing power networks, making the industry ecosystem increasingly diverse. Simultaneously, the rapid iteration of large-scale model technology imposes higher demands on the availability, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness of computing power. Against this backdrop, constructing a computing power service system from a user perspective, achieving efficient integration and scheduling of resources through computing power networks, and addressing the industrial transformation driven by the surge in inference demand have become urgent challenges for the computing power industry.
